overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. Informal meetings during drafting of the Town's TDR Bylaw were not meetings of a public body, so no minutes were required.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board created a working group that deliberated on Bylaw revisions outside an open meeting, citing dates on the draft Bylaw.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the meetings on December 5, 2013 and January 21, 2014 were not meetings of a public body, thus the individuals involved were not required to hold open meetings or keep minutes of their discussions.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to respond to a records request for agendas and minutes for meetings on dates listed on the draft Bylaw.
allegations.key_passage: Because we find that no public body participated in the development of the Bylaw, we also find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to provide the complainant with minutes as requested.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
